subject: Request: Availability exception and monthly credit calibration
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@healthsync.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Lee <alex.lee@cloudops.co>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability exception request for pilot + credit calculation example

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency improvements look promising. As we scoped our pilot we identified a pattern where our nightly aggregation jobs create sustained higher load on your hosted inference during a 3–4 hour window. Ops is worried that the standard 99.9% monthly uptime expectation will trigger credits for behavior that is an expected part of our workload.

Can we request a temporary availability exception for the pilot (3 months, then reassess) to a 99.5% monthly uptime floor with a capped monthly service credit structure? Procurement also asked for a sample credit calculation so they can model cost impact. I attached our SLA request form and an initial MAP worksheet showing peak windows and token distribution.

Key asks:
- Temporary uptime floor: 99.5% for pilot months
- Monthly credit cap: proposal from HealthSync — we asked for an example from Redwood
- Evidence/controls: what operational metrics or mitigations you need from our side to approve this?

Procurement contact: procurement@healthsync.com (cc'd in follow-ups).

Appreciate your help — if useful, Alex (cc) from our cloud team can share workload traces.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Infrastructure
HealthSync

Attachments: HealthSync_SLA_Request_Form.pdf, MAP_HealthSync_v1.xlsx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability exception request for pilot + credit calculation example

Hi Samira — thanks for the details and the MAP. Looping in Marissa (AM) and Connor (ops/legal) to help scope a short-term amendment.

High-level thoughts we can move on quickly:
1) Temporary exception window: we can support a 3-month pilot exception to 99.5% as requested, with an automatic review at the end of month 3. We typically require a mutually agreed MAP with clear acceptance criteria and signal definitions.
2) Credit mechanics: Redwood proposes an escrow-style monthly credit that accrues but is capped at 15% of monthly recurring hosted fees for the pilot. We can walk through a worked example once you confirm baseline monthly usage (avg tokens/day).
3) Evidence & mitigations: we need (a) consolidated hourly p95 request counts for your peak window, (b) confirmation of any prefix caching opportunities, and (c) confirmation that batch windows are scheduled and predictable.

I've attached a draft amendment (Redwood_SLA_Amendment_Draft.docx) that captures the 3-month exception, the credit cap approach, and an MAP stub. Marissa — can you take lead on the credit example and finance cap? Connor — can you advise on any legal flags around temporary SLA relaxations and the rollback clause?

If this looks good to Samira's team we'll prepare a short form amendment and a one-page credit example for procurement.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Amendment_Draft.docx

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@healthsync.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Lee <alex.lee@cloudops.co>, HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability exception request for pilot + credit calculation example

Thanks — this is helpful. A few answers from our side:
- Baseline usage: Avg 12M tokens/day across the account, peak nightly window accounts for ~30% of daily tokens. I'll attach the raw hourly p95 traces after I scrub a couple of hostnames.
- We can commit to a MAP that includes a scheduled maintenance window for heavy batches between 02:00–06:00 PST; those windows are predictable.
- Procurement asks for the worked example showing (a) credit when monthly uptime falls between 99.0–99.5 and (b) the cap mechanics. Can you include a numeric example with our baseline so we can show treasury?

We agree to the 3-month pilot and an automatic rollback to standard SLA after review unless both parties sign an extension. One operational question: will Redwood require any changes to how we tag requests / pass metadata to allow prefix caching? Alex can implement headers if that's needed.

Samira

On Thu, Mar 18, 2027 at 11:05 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> [Quoted earlier message and draft amendment attached]

Attachments to follow: hourly_p95_traces.csv (will share by end of day)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Availability exception request for pilot + credit calculation example

Evelyn / Connor — quick internal note after reviewing the MAP and Samira's baseline:

- Credit worked example: using HealthSync baseline (12M tokens/day, estimated monthly hosted bill = $42,000), if uptime dips into the 99.0–99.5 band we propose the following illustrative remedy: 10% credit of monthly hosted fees for that month for a single qualifying month. With our 15% cap, the max payable credit would be min(0.10 * $42,000, 0.15 * $42,000) = $4,200. I'll produce the one-page example for the procurement team (numbers + table).
- Finance wants the cap language explicit: "monthly remedy payable shall not exceed 15% of monthly hosted fees for the account during the pilot period."
- Connor: please verify the rollback clause language. We should require a 14-day notice prior to any permanent SLA change post-pilot. Also want a short clause stating Redwood can terminate the exception earlier if the pattern causes measurable impact to other customers.

I'll draft the one-pager and circulate to Samira; once they confirm the hourly traces we'll finalize. Approve me to share the draft amendment as a short form (no PII) with procurement?

Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
